intelligence.essence: Revocation Linearization Law: an evidence revocation has one authoritative commit point. Every later certification, projection publication and consequential execution must respect the new eligibility state. Asynchronous projection repair cannot weaken the rule. Independent support may establish a newer qualification; cached history cannot restore an older one. Three properties hold simultaneously — Safety: no post-revocation stale certification; Recovery: delayed replay cannot roll back current truth; Preservation: independent valid conclusions remain usable. The key is one authoritative ordering boundary, not one giant synchronous refresh. Historical intelligence survives, newer revocations win, and only current independently supported qualifications can become authoritative — even with crashed workers, delayed messages, concurrent writers and offline successors.
intelligence.falsifier: A stale publication winning a race against a committed revocation; a validation begun before R authorizing an action committed after R; a recovery worker applying event 22 over canonical revision 23; wall-clock timestamps ordering versions; an external action claimed revocable-safe without executor participation; a display presenting an overlapping-response as current without revalidation or invalidation coordination.

human_view.meaning: There's exactly one moment when a revocation becomes real — its commit — and everything after that moment must respect it. Every race gets a ruling: if the revocation won, the old publication dies; if the publication won, it was valid then but loses authority now; a check done before the revocation can't authorize an action taken after it. Recovery workers are janitors, not judges: they clean up against the current truth, never restore old verdicts. And for the most dangerous race — check, then revoke, then act — the action itself gets re-checked at the moment of commitment. Where the outside world won't cooperate, we say so honestly instead of claiming safety we can't enforce.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the formal bedrock under the whole correction discipline: SN-0783/0784/0785 describe WHAT must happen; the linearization law proves WHEN it happened with a single ordering that every component respects. The certification-safety vs display-freshness distinction is the permanent guard against overclaiming: we guarantee no authoritative certification through revoked evidence, and we label — never certify — anything that might be an overlapping response. The honest external-service limitation is the template for all safety claims: state exactly which boundary the guarantee covers.

intelligence.measurement_contract: Model-checked concurrent histories against ∀C,t: CertifiedCurrent(C,t) ⇒ AdmissibleSufficientSupport(C,t) with t as the authoritative linearization point: revocation-before-publication → rejected; publication-before-revocation → nonauthoritative after R; validation-before-R + action-after-R → revalidate or reject; recovery replays R after requalification → cannot overwrite; crash after R before notifications → enforced, outbox replays; two concurrent revocations → both represented; concurrent replacement evidence → newer valid qualification permitted; offline successor → history allowed, current certification prohibited; stale index pointer → serving refuses; eligibility source unavailable → fail closed. Plus transaction-isolation tests: no write skew, no stale-replica reads, no ABA version reuse. The deterministic fixture: one eligibility guard, one projection head, two writers, one revocation, one replay worker — ordering and stale-write rejection proven in isolation first.

naya_view.directive: Order every revocation, publication, validation, action, and recovery event on the single authoritative ≺ timeline. Establish the fence atomically inside the revocation transaction. Publish only through the atomic transaction with the full dependency predicate. Validate reads against linearizable state; distinguish certification safety from display freshness. Fence consequential actions at the commit boundary; state the covered boundary honestly for external effects. Replay recovery against canonical state, never as blind restoration. Model-check histories, not just functions.

simple_view.meaning: One moment makes a revocation real. Everything after respects it. Nothing old can sneak back into authority — not a late writer, not a crashed worker, not a restored backup.

intelligence.successor_effect: A cold successor inherits the linearization discipline: it orders its inherited history on the authoritative timeline and can never promote a pre-revocation qualification to current authority.
